governing_table.code: International Plumbing Code, adopted as part of the Alabama State Building Code (Ala. Admin. Code r. 355-12-1-.01); the same table is IBC Table 2902.1
governing_table.quote: Plumbing fixtures shall be provided in the minimum number as shown in Table 403.1, based on the actual use of the building or space.
governing_table.scope_note: Not a statewide code for all buildings. DCM: 'The State Building Code is limited to any new construction, addition, renovation ... on state-owned property and/or using state funds, on all public and private kindergarten through twelfth grade (K-12) schools, on public postsecondary schools, on hotels/motels and on movie theaters. ... DCM does not have jurisdiction over residential property or commercial property except for hotels/motels and movie theaters.' (https://dcm.alabama.gov/bldg_code.aspx). Private offices and restaurants follow the code their city or county adopted. No official page read says which model code most Alabama cities use.
governing_table.adoption_quote: The minimum building standard code adopted by the Division of Construction Management is the 2021 International Building Code. The following 2021 International Codes and companion codes are adopted: ... (c) 2021 - International Plumbing Code
governing_table.amendments: The official rule lists no Alabama change to IPC Chapter 4 or IBC Chapter 29 (its IBC exceptions touch only flammable gas, Table 307.1(1), 307.4, 307.5 and 414). UpCodes labels the Alabama Plumbing Code 2021 'Adopts Without Amendments'.

office.row_label: 2 Business: Buildings for the transaction of business, professional services, other services involving merchandise, office buildings, banks, ambulatory care, light industrial and similar uses
office.wc_male: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50
office.wc_female: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50
office.urinals: See Section 424.2 (may replace up to 50% of required water closets)
office.quote: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50

restaurant.row_label: 1 Assembly: Restaurants, banquet halls and food courts (footnote d)
restaurant.urinals: See Section 424.2 (may replace up to 67% of required water closets)
restaurant.quote: Restaurants, banquet halls and food courts d | 1 per 75 | 1 per 75 | 1 per 200

school.urinals: See Section 424.2 (may replace up to 67% of required water closets)
school.quote: Educational facilities | 1 per 50 | 1 per 50 | — | 1 per 100 | 1 service sink

sex_split.text: Total occupant load is divided in half, unless approved statistics show a different split.
sex_split.quote: To determine the occupant load of each sex, the total occupant load shall be divided in half. ... Exceptions: The total occupant load shall not be required to be divided in half where approved statistical data indicate a distribution of the sexes of other than 50 percent of each sex.

rounding.text: Fractions round up to the next whole number, for each sex.
rounding.quote: Fractional numbers resulting from applying the fixture ratios of Table 403.1 shall be rounded up to the next whole number.

urinal_substitution.text: Urinals are optional. In each toilet room they may replace up to 67% of the required toilets in assembly (restaurant) and educational buildings and up to 50% elsewhere. Each urinal needs a privacy partition.
urinal_substitution.quote: In each bathroom or toilet room, urinals shall not be substituted for more than 67 percent of the required water closets in assembly and educational occupancies. Urinals shall not be substituted for more than 50 percent of the required water closets in all other occupancies.

small_occupancy_exception.text: Separate men's and women's rooms are not required where the total occupant load is 15 or fewer, in business occupancies of 25 or fewer, or in mercantile occupancies of 100 or fewer.
small_occupancy_exception.quote: Separate facilities shall not be required in structures or tenant spaces with a total occupant load, including both employees and customers, of 15 or fewer. Separate facilities shall not be required in mercantile occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 100 or fewer. Separate facilities shall not be required in business occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 25 or fewer.

occupant_load.text: IBC Table 1004.5: business areas 150 gross sq ft per occupant; assembly without fixed seats, unconcentrated (tables and chairs) 15 net; educational classroom area 20 net.
occupant_load.quote: Unconcentrated (tables and chairs) | 15 net ... Business areas | 150 gross ... Educational | Classroom area | 20 net

stall_required.text: Each toilet used by the public or employees needs its own compartment with a door; each urinal needs partitions.
stall_required.quote: Each water closet utilized by the public or employees shall occupy a separate compartment with walls or partitions and a door enclosing the fixtures to ensure privacy.

worked_examples.how: 25 women, 25 men. 1 per 25 for the first 50: 25/25 = 1 each. Urinals may replace up to 50% of 1 = 0.5, so none.
50 women, 50 men. 50/25 = 2 each. Urinals may replace up to 50% of 2 = 1.
100 women, 100 men. First 50: 2; remaining 50 at 1 per 50: 1; total 3 each. Urinals up to 50% of 3 = 1.5, so 1.
200 women, 200 men. First 50: 2; remaining 150 at 1 per 50: 3; total 5 each. Urinals up to 50% of 5 = 2.5, so 2.
25 each. 25/75 = 0.33, rounds up to 1 each. Urinals up to 67% of 1 = 0.67, so none.
50 each. 50/75 = 0.67, rounds up to 1 each. Urinals up to 67% of 1 = 0.67, so none.
100 each. 100/75 = 1.33, rounds up to 2 each. Urinals up to 67% of 2 = 1.34, so 1.
200 each. 200/75 = 2.67, rounds up to 3 each. Urinals up to 67% of 3 = 2.01, so 2.
25 each. 25/50 = 0.5, rounds up to 1 each. Urinals up to 67% of 1 = 0.67, so none.
50 each. 50/50 = 1 each. Urinals up to 67% of 1 = 0.67, so none.
100 each. 100/50 = 2 each. Urinals up to 67% of 2 = 1.34, so 1.
200 each. 200/50 = 4 each. Urinals up to 67% of 4 = 2.68, so 2.

fixtures.worked_examples_note: The urinal limit applies 'in each bathroom or toilet room'; the figures assume one men's room holds all the men's fixtures.

hdpe_fire.section: 2021 IBC Section 803.9 (with 803.1.1 and 803.1.1.1), as adopted in the Alabama State Building Code; the same sentence is 2021 International Fire Code Section 803.9, which the State Fire Marshal adopts as a statewide regulation (Ala. Admin. Code r. 482-2-101-.02)
hdpe_fire.quote: 803.9 High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE) and Polypropylene (PP). Where high-density polyethylene or polypropylene is used as an interior finish, it shall comply with Section 803.1.1. | 803.1.1 Interior wall and ceiling finish materials shall be classified in accordance with NFPA 286 and comply with Section 803.1.1.1. | Chapter 2, Interior Wall and Ceiling Finish: The exposed interior surfaces of buildings, including but not limited to: fixed or movable walls and partitions; toilet room privacy partitions; ...
hdpe_fire.note: IBC text applies within the State Building Code's scope (state-owned or state-funded buildings, K-12 schools, public colleges, hotels, motels, movie theaters). Fire Marshal rule: 'the 2021 edition of the International Fire Code and Appendices B, C, D, E, and M ... are adopted by reference as a regulation of the State Fire Marshal.' Cities enforce their own adopted editions for other buildings. Code sections read on UpCodes (secondary); adoption read on official pages.

access.state_standard: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design, adopted directly as part of the State Building Code in place of IBC Chapter 11 accessibility requirements and ANSI/ICC A117.1 (Ala. Admin. Code r. 355-12-1-.01(1)(i) and (2)). Alabama has no separate state accessibility code.
access.differences_note: None. The state adopts the federal standard itself, so stall, door, toe clearance, grab bar, children's stall and sign rules are the federal ones.
access.quote: The requirements of the 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design supersede the accessibility requirements contained in the International Building Code and ANSI A117.1.
access.process: No state registration or fee step for private commercial projects. The Division of Construction Management (DCM) reviews plans for buildings in its scope (state-owned or state-funded, K-12 schools, public colleges, hotels, motels, movie theaters) and, for city and county owned projects, only for ADA: 'DCM's code jurisdiction over plans and specifications of all municipal and county-owned projects is limited to such projects meeting Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Standards.' (https://dcm.alabama.gov/bldg_code.aspx)

single_user.rule: Within the State Building Code's scope, single-user toilet rooms count toward the required fixtures and must be identified as available to everyone regardless of sex. No Alabama statute on single-user restroom signs was found. For private buildings outside that scope the city's adopted code decides.
single_user.quote: Single-user toilet and bathing rooms, and family or assisted-use toilet rooms and bathing rooms shall be identified as being available for use by all persons regardless of their sex.

all_gender_shared.rule: The 2021 code as adopted allows a shared room for all genders: every toilet in its own compartment with a door, and urinals in stalls or in a visually separated area; the fixture count is then worked out on the total occupant load. In public K-12 schools and public colleges state law requires multiple occupancy restrooms to be designated by sex (see use_restrictions).
all_gender_shared.quote: Separate facilities shall not be required where rooms having both water closets and lavatory fixtures are designed for use by both sexes and privacy for water closets is provided in accordance with Section 405.3.4. Urinals shall be located in an area visually separated from the remainder of the facility or each urinal that is provided shall be located in a stall. | Where multiple-user facilities are designed to serve all genders, the minimum fixture count shall be calculated 100 percent, based on total occupant load. In such multiple-user facilities, each fixture type shall be in accordance with ICC A117.1 and each urinal that is provided shall be located in a stall.

use_restrictions.rule: (1) Public K-12 schools: Ala. Code 16-1-54 (Act 2022-290) requires multiple occupancy restrooms and changing areas designated for student use to be used according to biological sex as stated on the original birth certificate. (2) Public colleges and universities: Act 2024-34 (SB129), effective October 1, 2024 per secondary sources, requires every multiple occupancy restroom to be designated by biological sex. (3) SB79 of 2025 (enrolled) says the state and its political subdivisions are not prohibited from establishing single-sex spaces; it sets no restroom mandate. No statute was found covering private buildings or city and county buildings generally.
use_restrictions.quote: Each public institution of higher education shall ensure that every multiple occupancy restroom be designated for use by individuals based on their biological sex, as defined by Section 16-1-54, Code of Alabama 1975. (SB129 Enrolled, 2024) | (1) BIOLOGICAL SEX. The physical condition of being male or female, as stated on the individual's original birth certificate. (Section 16-1-54(a) as reproduced in SB79 Introduced, 2025) | Neither the state nor any political subdivision of the state shall be prohibited from establishing separate single-sex spaces or environments for males and females when biology, privacy, safety, or fairness are implicated. (SB79 Enrolled, 2025)
use_restrictions.note: The operative sentence of 16-1-54(b) was not read on a clean official copy (the legislature's code site needs JavaScript; Justia and LegiScan refused). SB79 Introduced reproduces it mixed with proposed changes; read as existing law it says a public K-12 school shall require every multiple occupancy restroom or changing area designated for student use to be used by individuals based on their biological sex.

public_wage.law: None. Alabama's prevailing wage law was repealed in 1980. Only the federal Davis-Bacon Act applies, on federally funded or assisted construction.
public_wage.note: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division, 'Dollar Threshold Amount for Contract Coverage' (last revised January 1, 2023), read through the fetch tool; direct download was refused. The federal Davis-Bacon threshold and sam.gov rates were not read in this pass.

shipped_goods.rule: An out-of-state seller with more than $250,000 a year of retail sales into Alabama must register and collect. It may use the Simplified Sellers Use Tax: a flat 8% on all sales into Alabama, whatever the delivery city, in place of state and local rates. If the seller collects nothing, the buyer owes consumers use tax at the state sales tax rate, and city or county rates may also apply.
shipped_goods.quote: An out-of-state seller who is making retail sales of tangible personal property into the state is required to register with the Department and to collect and remit tax ... when the seller's retail sales of tangible personal property sold into the state exceed $250,000 per year based on the previous calendar year's sales. (Rule 810-6-2-.90.03) | a flat 8 percent sellers use tax on all sales made into Alabama ... The flat tax applies to all sales regardless of the locality shipped to in Alabama. (ALDOR SSUT page)

freight.rule: Freight by common carrier is not taxed if billed as a separate item and paid by the buyer. It is taxed if folded into 'shipping and handling' or if the seller delivers in its own or leased equipment.
freight.quote: Where delivery of tangible personal property is made by common carrier or the U. S. Postal Service, the transportation charges shall not be subject to sales or use tax if billed as a separate item and paid directly or indirectly by the purchaser. ... Transportation charges are not separate and identifiable if included with other charges and billed as "shipping and handling" or "postage and handling".

install_labor.rule: A seller's installation charge is not taxed when shown separately on the bill and in the seller's books. A lump-sum price for goods and installation is taxed in full.
install_labor.quote: Where the quoted or advertised price is a lump sum for both property and installation or where billing and other records do not show separate charges for property and for installation, the measure of the tax is the total amount received by the seller. ... he may make a separate and additional charge for making the installation which, when shown separately in his billings and on his books, will not be subject to the sales tax.

furnish_and_install.rule: A contractor who attaches building materials to real property is the consumer: the contractor pays sales or use tax when buying the materials and does not charge sales tax on the contract. Materials for contracts with governmental entities can be exempt (Rule 810-6-3-.77). The rule does not name toilet partitions; it covers 'any and all other tangible personal property which becomes a part of real property'.
furnish_and_install.quote: Contractors or builders must pay either to the seller or directly to the Department of Revenue sales or use tax on the following: ... (b) All building materials attached by them to real property except property qualifying for a specific exemption. (Rule 810-6-1-.46) | Building materials when purchased by builders, contractors or landowners for use in adding to, repairing, or altering real property are subject to either the sales or use tax at the time of purchase by such builder, contractor, or landowner. (Rule 810-6-1-.27)

page.stalls_intro: Alabama's state building rules count toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. Half are counted as men and half as women, and fractions round up. Every toilet needs a stall. Urinals are optional: in a men's room they may replace up to two thirds of the toilets in a restaurant or school and up to half in an office, and each urinal needs a privacy screen.
page.stalls_after: The state rules apply to schools, hotels, movie theaters and state-owned or state-funded buildings. A private office or restaurant follows the building rules its city or county has adopted, so confirm the count with the local building department. These are minimums for the whole building, and at least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, the state rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20.
page.fire_bullet: - **Fire safety:** Alabama's state building and fire rules require solid plastic (HDPE) partitions to pass a room fire test. Ask for the fire-rated version.
page.access_bullet: - **Wheelchair access:** a restroom with stalls needs at least one stall a wheelchair user can enter and use. Alabama uses the federal access rules as its own, so one set of sizes applies. The state reviews plans for schools, hotels, movie theaters and state-funded buildings, and checks city and county owned projects for access.
page.state_extra_bullet: - **Alabama and federal stall rules match:** Alabama adopted the federal access rules in place of a state version, so a stall that meets the federal rules meets the state's.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** under the state building rules a one-person restroom is marked as open to everyone, and a shared all-gender room is allowed if every toilet sits in its own compartment with a door and urinals are in stalls or screened from view. Alabama law requires shared restrooms in public K-12 schools and public colleges to be designated for one sex.
page.public_jobs: Alabama has no state wage law for public jobs, so a set wage applies only on federally funded work.
page.tax_install_bullet: - **Tax on installation:** in Alabama, an installation charge shown separately on the bill is not taxed. A single price for partitions and installation is taxed in full when a seller installs what it sells. A contractor who supplies and installs under a construction contract pays the tax on the materials instead of charging it to you.
page.tax_ship_bullet: - **Buying without installation:** partitions shipped to {city} are taxable. An out-of-state seller in Alabama's simplified program collects a flat 8% in place of state and local tax. Freight by common carrier is not taxed when it is billed as a separate line. If the seller doesn't collect the tax, the buyer owes it to the state.
page.tax_confirm: your accountant or the Alabama Department of Revenue
